hypothesis: A learned permutation-equivariant hypergraph representation of conflicts between public-consistent causal operator worlds will generalize to unfamiliar longer shared-binding programs and select certificate-critical queries with strict savings versus equally trained static baselines, while preserving exact correctness and complete resource nonregression.

mechanism.representation: Eight public-consistent S3 assignments are vertices; output-disagreeing pairs become typed conflict hyperedges whose role-difference support is the hyperedge incidence. A role's feature is aggregations of unresolved conflict hyperedges by cardinality, branch-resolved conflict mass, immediate post-observation certificate likelihood, and pairwise structural message channels. This is not a role-name weight or adjustable query-priority scalar.
mechanism.trainable: Global permutation-equivariant linear message aggregation coefficients trained by supervised optimization on TRAIN-only exact public counterfactual optimal decisions across legal partial observations. No actual private operator, private truth, DEV case or DEV response can supply a training gradient.
mechanism.inference: At each actual purchased observation, filter public-consistent worlds, compute conflict hyperedges, rank unqueried role through TRAIN-learned graph message coefficients and acquire one real second calibration pair. Every termination requires exact output equality over all remaining public-consistent worlds; never predict an answer from learned scores alone.
mechanism.soundness: Cross-check certificate candidate with unchanged exact S3 public operator semantics on source-free algebraic properties before any DEV evaluation. If unresolved after all live roles purchased use exact certified fallback, never guess.

source.source_birth: self-authored original synthetic new longer commutator/conjugation grammar; no reuse of T19, T20 or T21A source; not independent
source.train_and_dev_grammar: TRAIN 8-14-token repeated-binding commutator motifs, DEV 15-23-token layered commutator+conjugation programs. They may share public operator vocabulary but no instances/seeds.
source.privacy: All candidate and trained comparator models get public first calibration pairs, word, start and authenticated second pairs only after a counted request; scoring harness alone knows actual operator and truth.

controls.training_parity: All TRAIN-informed arms see same 72 public TRAIN cases and legal public counterfactual worlds; compare strongest TRAIN-informed fixed order, not only untrained baseline.
controls.oracle: Exact adaptive DP is an upper bound on query-selection performance on the known finite public S3 class; a learned method must never claim a query advantage over that oracle. Its value would instead be smaller complete inference cost, if demonstrated.
controls.evaluation: 64 or more untouched DEV problems, exact correctness on all arms, five fresh whole-process OS repetitions including training/source construction, record median process CPU, peak RSS, purchased queries, number of model weights/updates and service cost when measurable.

preregistered_acceptance.technical: source hashes and freeze ancestry verified, 0 wrong answers, 0 masked unknowns, all 5 arms and 5 processes on Linux and Windows, original run+artifact receipts
preregistered_acceptance.claimed_learned_transfer: Only if trained hypergraph strictly beats the best TRAIN-informed static comparator in aggregate purchased queries across both OS, remains exact, and complete CPU/RSS/query-service do not regress versus equally informed T16B AND static AND fixed exact adaptive. Independent source-born first-use replication further required for scientific/optimizer admission.
preregistered_acceptance.if_negative: Seal original result and stop source reuse; do not tune coefficients on consumed DEV. This mechanism remains a developmental negative.
preregistered_acceptance.known_shortcoming: All operator vocabulary S3 is supplied to public exact verifier, so gains cannot establish transfer to genuinely unknown causal semantics.
